Dear Acting Administrator Carlson: 

On October 19, 2023, the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) published in 

the Federal Register a Notice and request for comments on a request for approval of a new 

information collection (NPRM) seeking approval to conduct a one-time voluntary study to obtain 

information to better understand attitudes and behaviors related to alcohol-impaired driving that will 

be used to enhance and refine communication strategy and tactics. The study will survey drivers and 

motorcycle riders ages 21- to 54-years-old because this age range represents the greatest number of 

alcohol-related driving/riding fatalities according to NHTSA's Fatality Analysis Reporting System 

(FARS). The National Association of Mutual Insurance Companies (NAMIC) welcomes the 

opportunity to respond to this request for comments. 

NAMIC is the largest property/casualty insurance trade group with a diverse membership of more 

than 1,500 local, regional, and national member companies, including seven of the top ten 

property/casualty insurers in the United States. NAMIC members lead the personal lines sector 

representing 55 percent of the auto market. Through our advocacy programs we promote public 

policy solutions that benefit NAMIC member companies and the policyholders they serve and foster 

greater understanding and recognition of the unique alignment of interests between management and 

policyholders of mutual companies.

 
The NPRM provides that the proposed research study will include two components, both being one-

time collections. The first component will involve a series of online webcam interviews that will 

collect qualitative information that will serve as a cognitive test to improve the quantitative survey 

that will be administered in the second component. The quantitative survey will be administered 

online and by phone. After collecting the data, segmentation analysis will be done to classify drivers 

and motorcycle riders according to segments based on common demographics, drinking behaviors, 

attitudes about drinking and driving/motorcycle riding, and lifestyle characteristics. The NHTSA's 

Office of Communications and Consumer Information will use segmentation profiles to better target 

and reach intended audiences with communications messages and techniques that are relevant and 

meaningful to people within the target market.

The Scarlet macaw is one of the most popular captive bred macaw species and has proliferated as a result of domestic husbandry. The Scarlet macaw is the 2nd most commonly kept pet macaw in the US following the Blue & Gold macaw. That alone speaks volumes for not listing it as endangered here in the US.

The Scarlet macaw was originally impacted due to deforestation and habitat loss in it's native environment, but conservation efforts in those countries have had a positive effect and the Scarlet macaw has proliferated as a result, and the population has recovered and is now considered stable. We have not imported Scarlet macaws since 1992 and the fact that they have produced so well domestically attests to their innate ability to adapt and survive in friendly & new environments and that they are not, in fact, an endangered species.

The Scarlet macaw is not endangered domestically, but it could become endangered in the US if listed on the ESA. There are 25 states where it is illegal to keep any species that is listed on the ESA, and pet owners & breeders in those states automatically become criminals unless they have a Captive Bred Wildlife Permit to breed and/or keep them. 

Listing the Scarlet macaw on the ESA is counter intuitive and counterproductive. Some breeders with recently listed ESA species have already closed off nest boxes and shut down breeding pairs from future production. Others have already turned to producing hybrids with their recently listed ESA species, including the Buffon's, Military and Blue-throated macaws. I write on behalf of the City Colleges of Chicago to support the proposal of the US Department of Education Office of Postsecondary Education to waive the requirements in the Education Department General Administrative Regulations that generally prohibit project periods exceeding five years and project period extensions involving the obligation of additional Federal funds. This proposed waiver and extension would have considerable and measurable positive impact on furthering the goals and objectives of the projects funded under CFDA number 84.382A. Additionally, as a large, urban community college district comprised of both Predominantly Black Institutions and Hispanic Serving Institutions, the waiver would enable the City Colleges of Chicago to strategically align applications for and (if funded) execution of these related Title III, Part F projects.

In September 2015, the US Department of Education awarded the Predominantly Black Institutions grant to Malcolm X College, one of the City Colleges of Chicago. The focus of this project has been to enable and support African-Americans to matriculate through the health sciences programs and concurrently provide them with the opportunities to either transfer into four-year institutions or graduate with credentials of economic value. Three primary goals of the grant have guided the activities of the project. By carrying out these activities, the College has made substantial progress toward accomplishing the overarching strategic goals: (1) to increase the number of students earning college credentials of economic value; (2) to increase the rate of transfer to Bachelor's degree programs following CCC graduation; and, (3) to drastically improve outcomes for students needing remediation. In this most recent project year alone, Malcolm X College was able to serve over 500 African American males through its Black Male Institute Conference. We accomplished this by extending our outreach to cultivate relationships with approximately 30 low-income and/or minority-serving public schools throughout the Cityof Chicago, and provide STEM programming for 5th-8th grade students.

As indicated above, the City Colleges of Chicago's support of this waiver is twofold. First, the opportunity to continue PBI activities at the City Colleges of Chicago would allow us to continue to strengthen the pipeline of Black students enrolling in and successfully completing higher education in the City of Chicago. It will allow us to continue to build the capacity of our institutions to serve those students as we groom them for success in higher education and for entry into the workforce. Second, it would enable the City Colleges of Chicago - and other similar districts - to coordinate districtwide efforts to align applications for the Title III, Part F discretionary grant programs for which their colleges are eligible.
